newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: New claims for jobless benefits posted a big drop last week, the government said Thursday, reversing much of a sharp gain the week before when carmakers laid off workers to retool plants for new models.
The Labour Department said the number of Americans filing for first-time unemployment insurance benefits dropped to 349,000 in the week ended July 12 from 377,000 the week before.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 345,000 in the July 12 week.
The four-week moving average, which smooths out weekly fluctuations in claims and is viewed as a more reliable gauge of employment trends, rose slightly to 348,750 from 348,500.
The average was the highest since the week ended Jan. 18, when claims reached 349,500, the department said.
The number of people continuing to file for claims fell to 2,378,000 from 2,388,000 in the week ended July 5, the latest period for which data were available.

The department said 15 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended July 5, the latest period for which those data were available.
Michigan had the largest increase in claims, reporting 21,002 due to layoffs as the automobile industry closed plants to retool.
Other states reporting large increases included New York, with 8,473 new claims, Ohio, with 7,154, Wisconsin, with 6,640, Indiana, with 5,574, Kentucky, with 5,277, and Arkansas, with 3,283.
New York reported layoffs in the service industry, while Ohio said it had layoffs in the transportation equipment industry and in various other industries throughout the state.
Wisconsin linked its rise in claims to layoffs in the service industry and in the manufacturing sector, while Indiana provided no explanation.
Kentucky said it had layoffs in the primary and fabricated metals, apparel, rubber and glass industries. Arkansas reported layoffs in the apparel, lumber and transportation equipment sectors.
Labour said three states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the July 5 week.
They were California, with 3,003 fewer filings, Massachusetts, with 2,053, and New Jersey, with 1,966.
California attributed the drop in claims to a shorter work week due to the Independence Day holiday. Massachusetts had no comment.
New Jersey also linked the decrease to a holiday-shortened work week as well as fewer layoffs in the trade, service and transportation industries.
